g.text: 10B Sensor fastening stacks and cable exits
Read each stack in order • no scanner load passes through the Pi or its header
Bridge feet — 4 joints
M3×16 head → washer → deck 4 → foot 6 → washer → M3 nyloc
Install from BELOW; fit both frames before boards obscure the upper nuts.
Bridge top — 4 joints
M3×16 head → washer → plate 4 → rail 6 → washer → M3 nyloc
Install from ABOVE; nuts remain accessible inside the side frames.
A1 scanner — 4 columns, conditional on model match
M3×10 + washer above foot 5 → M3 F/F column 35 → bridge 4 → washer + M3×10 below
Nominal thread engagement: 4.5 mm above / 5.5 mm below. Motor clears bridge by 8.5 mm.
WM8960 — 2 GPIO-side positions, conditional on seated gap
M2.5×16 from BELOW → washer → adapter 3 → spacer 6 → Pi 1.6 → washer → F/F pillar 12
Above: M2.5×6 → washer → HAT 1.6 → pillar. Natural board-face gap must match 12.5 mm.
Interface carrier — 2 columns
M2.5×8 + washer above bridge 4 → M2.5 F/F column 15 → carrier 3 → washer + M2.5×8
Board-specific insulated supports are still required; the bare PCB must not lie on screw heads.
Cable paths remain below the scanning plane
A1 cable: rear opening to P17, USB toward the left-side Pi ports. CSI: front bridge slots to a relaxed head loop.
Keep microphone openings and the open bridge windows uncovered. Check the entire head motion with the real ribbon.
P12 LiDAR bridge: lidar_bridge_s1.stl | P17 LiDAR interface carrier: lidar_interface_carrier_s1.stl
S0/S1 candidate • simplified assembly illustration • dimensions in mm • not a fabrication template
